source.title: Student Specialization in Deep ReLU Networks With Finite Width and Input Dimension

record.tranche_reason: The study measures student-to-teacher specialization using normalized activation correlations and recovery rates, rather than testing convergence with the original source's method.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses CCA/SVCCA and cites prior specialization results, but those discussions and cited findings are not study results. Rows below cover its own measurements of student specialization; other reported measures such as evaluation accuracy are not representation-alignment measures.
record.test_reason: Students of one architecture, trained from 32 random seeds against a fixed teacher, are scored on whether their units match the teacher's units (normalized activation correlation). This bears on V3: different initializations recover the same features, one-to-many, with leftover unspecialized units. It is indirect, because students are compared with a supervising teacher, not with each other. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The main contribution is theoretical: when the per-sample gradient is small, each lowest-layer teacher node is aligned with at least one student node, with polynomial sample complexity in the two-layer case. The authors also argue that strong teacher nodes specialize first, and that unspecialized students are prunable. Experiments show one-to-many specialization that improves with over-realization, more data and stronger teacher nodes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses teacher-student training and normalized activation correlations to assess neuron specialization; it does not test broad representational-distance convergence between independently trained models or compare similarity metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with sample count, layer, loss, over-realization, teacher-node strength, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: A student trained on a fixed teacher's outputs aligns its lowest-layer units with the teacher's units. This is alignment to a supervising network, not between independently trained models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-realized ReLU students trained to imitate a teacher recover the teacher's units one-to-many, with stronger (high fan-out) teacher units recovered first.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR 119, 2020)
record.problems: Most empirical alignment values are shown only in figures, without numerical estimates or uncertainty intervals. The experiments use a fixed teacher and do not test broad cross-architecture or cross-modal convergence. Deeper-network theory concerns the lowest layer, and the paper notes that its theory does not cover cross-entropy loss.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 7 also plots p=1, 1.5, 2, and 2.5 with 2x and 5x over-realization and the 5-epoch rates; these additional teacher-index curves were omitted to stay within the row limit. Figure 8's per-teacher-node training-dynamics curves were also omitted. Section 7 and Figures 7-8.

untested.parts: No direct student-to-student comparison across seeds. Convergence is inferred via a shared teacher. There is no test of shared subspaces versus differing bases.
Alignment is to a supervising teacher whose outputs are the training target, so it says nothing about partial convergence between independently trained models or its causes.
Single similarity measure; no comparison across metrics or input sets.

missing.what: Figure 3 toy 2D example: 6 students on 2 teachers. Fan-out norms of unaligned students drop to 0.01 or 0.00 by iteration 29.
Figure 8 per-teacher specialization dynamics: strong teachers specialize fast, weak ones slowly (declared in rows_left_out).

record.verdict_notes: V7 links were removed. Alignment here is to a teacher whose outputs are the training labels, so it cannot speak to whether independently trained models only partially converge or why. The V3 bearing is indirect: shared features across seeds are inferred because seeds converge to the same teacher units. Most values are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale and capability, or comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language comparison.

Tests students trained from different random seeds against a fixed teacher, not direct pairwise comparisons between students. It does not test whether individual units or bases differ while subspaces agree.
No direct test of mapping or stitching representations between models.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Uses normalized activation correlation; it does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings, or in-distribution and out-of-distribution inputs.

Reports incomplete specialization and dependence on training setup, but does not compare shared-data/objective explanations against a common-reality explanation or test whether alignment plateaus across model scale.

relationships.condition: Over-realized students (2x-10x), low teacher polarity, lowest layer, synthetic and CIFAR-10
relationships.reason: Across seeds, students specialize one-to-many onto the same teacher nodes, and unspecialized units get near-zero fan-out (r2-r4, r6, r9, r13, r25-r28).
relationships.display_finding: Student units specialized one-to-many onto the same teacher nodes across seeds, while unspecialized units acquired near-zero outgoing weights.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Over-realized students (2x-10x), low teacher polarity, lowest layer, synthetic and CIFAR-10
source_check.reason: One-to-many specialization and weak fan-out from unspecialized nodes support shared features under different initializations. The CIFAR-10 evidence uses a teacher pruned to retain strong nodes.

relationships.condition: 1x students, highly polarized (weak) teacher nodes, upper layers of deep nets
relationships.reason: Recovery is incomplete: weak teacher nodes go unmatched, 1x students get stuck, and upper layers converge worse than the lowest (r1, r7, r8, r10-r12, r14-r24).
relationships.display_finding: Weak teacher nodes remained unmatched, 1× students became stuck, and upper layers converged less successfully than the lowest layer.
